marta: Quick follow-up from the multi-region sync RFC — I sketched a local-first write + async-replicate fallback pattern for workloads with data residency constraints. Want to sanity-check tradeoffs before I turn it into a runbook. :thinking:

alex: OK show the sketch, curious about correctness/DR paths.

marta: High level: prefer local region for reads and writes for tenants with residency policy. Writes are acknowledged locally and enqueued for cross-region replication. If local region fails, traffic falls back to nearest region but we only allow fallback writes for tenants who've opted into cross-region replication (explicit consent).

marta: Config example for routing/policy:
```yaml
policies:
  - tenant_id: T123
    residency: EU-only
    local_write: true
    cross_region_replication: async
    allow_fallback_writes: false
```

jia: So for a EU-only tenant with allow_fallback_writes:false we would reject writes from outside EU during failover? That implies availability loss when EU region is down. Is that acceptable for those customers?

marta: Exactly. We want a clear tradeoff: strict residency -> stronger locality guarantees but possible partial outages. We can offer an "opt-in fallback" to trade availability for continuity.

kevin: Two operational concerns: 1) conflict resolution if async replication replays to other region where concurrent write occurred (rare for single-tenant but possible for multi-client). 2) KV cache invalidation across regions — stale reads if replication lag.

alex: For conflicts we can use last-writer-wins with vector of (region,id,timestamp) or use CRDTs for some data types. But CRDTs are heavier and not universally applicable. Agree we need an explicit conflict policy per table/obj.

marta: My thought: annotate models with "conflict_policy": [lww, merge-crdt, reject] so we can choose per domain. Defaults to lww for metadata, merge-crdt for counters.

jia: For read staleness we should expose SLA: e.g., 95% of cross-region replication within X seconds on Dedicated vs hosted best-effort. Also add a cache-coherency header so clients can decide to force strong read-after-write by routing to write-region if needed.

kevin: Agree about headers. Something like `X-Read-Consistency: local|write-region|strong` and SDK helpers. Make it explicit rather than magic.

marta: Another piece: legal requirement mapping. We need tenant-level flags plus an audit trail proving writes never left-region (for strict mode). That means for strict "EU-only" we must disable any proxying and block background replication unless backed by customer contract.

deploy-bot: Deployment note: rolling update strategy for replication worker changes must avoid double-apply during overlap windows. Use worker idempotency keys: `replica_op:{tenant}:{seq}`.

alex: Good call. Also think about observability: expose per-tenant replication lag, replication queue depth, and a boolean "is_fallback_enabled" on tenant page. SRE can set alerts when lag>threshold and fallback attempted.

marta: Action items: 1) I'll draft a small runbook for strict vs opt-in fallback tenants. 2) @alex and @kevin can you propose a minimal conflict policy table? 3) @jia can you add suggested SDK header surface?

alex: Yep, I'll draft conflict_policy table by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:

jia: On it — will propose headers and SDK behavior.

kevin: I'll sketch worker idempotency and cache invalidation notes.

marta: Thanks — if no objections I'll convert this thread into a short RFC + runbook and ping security/compliance for the audit wording.

alex: No objections. go for it.

marta: Cool, will follow up with PR.
